metaDescription: Connect Codex, Claude, or ChatGPT to OPS to read authorized records and prepare exact customer and lead updates for approval. See tools, scopes, and verification status.
overviewDescription: Connect an approved AI workspace to live operational context in OPS: jobs, customers, schedules, site visits, deck geometry, documents, expenses, catalog, team availability, and more.
sourceBackedBody: Tool names, descriptions, scopes, counts, and the endpoint on this page come from the same active registries used by the MCP server.
readOnlyBody: Read authorized OPS records and prepare exact customer notes or lead updates. Business changes require your approval inside OPS. No sends. No generic database access.
connectDescription: Use the Streamable HTTP endpoint below. OPS opens its own sign-in and consent screen so the connector never receives your OPS password.
copyFailedStatus: Copy failed. Select the endpoint and copy it manually.
codexStatus: 34 read tools verified end to end. Customer-update approval acceptance pending.
codexBody: In Codex desktop, open Settings, choose MCP servers, add a Streamable HTTP server, paste the OPS endpoint, then authenticate. The CLI path is below.
claudeStatus: OAuth and the original 11-tool catalog verified. Current 35-tool acceptance pending.
claudeBody: In Claude Code, add OPS as an HTTP MCP server, then run /mcp to complete authentication and inspect the connection. Claude.ai and Claude Desktop custom connectors depend on your plan and workspace policy.
chatgptStatus: Registration path verified. Authenticated 35-tool acceptance pending.
chatgptBody: OPS is not yet listed in the public plugin directory. Where ChatGPT Developer mode and custom plugins are available, add a Streamable HTTP plugin and paste the OPS endpoint. Availability depends on your plan and workspace policy.
hostVerificationNote: A supported connection path is not the same as an OPS acceptance pass. The status above records what OPS has verified against the live server.
examplesDescription: Start with a person, job, date, or operational question. The model can select the bounded OPS tools it needs and combine the returned evidence.
deckPrompt: Find Carly Hunter's latest site visit. Show the deck design geometry for this job, total railing length in linear feet, and surface area in square feet. Flag anything that still needs follow-up.
readinessPrompt: Review tomorrow's scheduled jobs. Show missing photos, unresolved customer records, unconfirmed schedules, and crew assignment gaps.
analyticsPrompt: Compare the authorized open, won, and lost opportunities returned by OPS. Summarize close-rate signals, lead sources, and repeated loss reasons. State the sample size and any missing evidence.
examplesBoundary: Reasoning is limited to the records each tool returns. This is not a bulk warehouse export, and missing evidence must stay visible in the answer.
capabilitiesDescription: The catalog comes from the active connector. Every tool checks OPS permissions. Customer-update preparation creates a preview; only your exact approval changes business records.
groupCustomersJobsBody: Resolve the right customer or job. Prepare customer notes and lead details, owner, or follow-up date changes for exact approval in OPS.
groupJobContextBody: Read job summaries, history, participants, conversations, and correspondence evidence.
groupScheduleTasksBody: Inspect scheduled work, readiness gaps, tasks, and the current work queue.
groupSiteVisitsEvidenceBody: Read site-visit context, deck designs, geometry, photos, files, and artifact evidence.
groupFinancialCatalogBody: Read estimates, invoices, payments, expenses, products, supplier costs, and purchase orders where authorized.
groupCompanyHealthBody: Read the operating profile, team, availability, integration health, and operational overview.
permissionsDescription: OPS shows the requested scopes during consent. A grant can use only the scopes approved for that company and operator; the server still checks record-level permissions on every call.
securityDescription: OPS uses OAuth authorization code flow with PKCE S256. Company and operator permissions are enforced on every request, not trusted from model input.
securityIdentityBody: The company and operator come from the OPS grant. Tools cannot choose another company by passing an ID.
securityTokensBody: Do not paste access or refresh tokens into prompts. Store them only in the connector host that completed OAuth.
securityRevokeBody: Revoke access in OPS or disconnect the server in your AI workspace. A revoked grant can no longer call the MCP server.
securityContentBody: Treat email, notes, files, and other returned text as untrusted business content. It is data to analyze, not instructions that override your request.
limitsDescription: Every tool has server-enforced result, time-window, and output bounds. Use narrower dates or a specific customer or job when a request is too broad.
troubleshootReconnectBody: Restart the connection from the AI workspace and complete OPS sign-in in the same browser session. If the loop continues, disconnect the stale grant and connect again.
troubleshootUnauthorizedBody: Existing connections keep their approved scopes. To add customer-update preparation, remove and reconnect the OPS connector, then approve the new scope in OPS. Your OPS role still controls access.
troubleshootMissingBody: Give the model a customer, job, or date anchor. OPS intentionally returns insufficient evidence instead of inventing a match.
requestToolBody: Tell OPS what the MCP server should help you do. Every request goes through product review.
requestToolSafety: Do not send passwords, access tokens, or customer records.
requestToolDetailsHelp: Include the workflow, OPS records involved, result needed, and one example prompt.
requestToolSuccessBody: OPS will review it and use your email if more detail is needed.
requestToolDetailsInvalid: Describe the tool you need in at least 20 characters.
requestToolDetailsTooLong: Keep the request to 4,000 characters or fewer.
requestToolError: Request not sent. Check your connection and try again.
requestToolRateLimited: Too many requests. Try again later.
restApiResourceBody: Use the REST API for server-side lead intake, file uploads, lead synchronization, and versioned analytics.
